title: API 580 Training in Baton Rouge: RBI Exam Prep Online
description: Self-paced online API 580 exam prep for RBI planners and engineers at Baton Rouge refineries and Geismar and Plaquemine chemical plants, with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 580 Training in Baton Rouge: Risk Based Inspection Exam Prep for Refinery, Chlor-Alkali and Nitrogen Plant RBI Teams
html:
API 580 exam prep for risk-based inspection teams on the Baton Rouge corridor

Risk-based inspection decides where a plant spends its inspection effort, and on the Mississippi between Baton Rouge and Donaldsonville that decision covers refinery units, chlor-alkali and vinyls plants, methanol and ammonia trains, polymer plants and the tank fields and docks that serve them. API 580 certifies that a person understands the RBI method described in API RP 580. This page is for the inspection planners, corrosion and materials engineers, reliability engineers and inspection supervisors on the corridor who are preparing for that examination.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Baton Rouge. The API 580 course is self-paced and online, and an instructor answers your questions while you work through it. The American Petroleum Institute sets the eligibility rules, administers the API 580 examination at a test centre or, where API offers it, by remote proctoring, and issues the certification. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and the course on its own confers no credential.

Who sits API 580 between Baton Rouge and Donaldsonville

  • Certified inspectors moving into planning. Holders of a current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification qualify for API 580 automatically, and many plant inspectors add it when they take on an RBI role.
  • Corrosion and materials engineers. They write the damage mechanism basis behind every corrosion loop, and API 580 covers how that basis feeds the probability side of the model.
  • Reliability and mechanical integrity engineers. In chemical plants the RBI programme often sits with the reliability group rather than a separate inspection department.
  • RBI software analysts and contractors. People who run assessments in commercial software benefit from the vendor-neutral grounding RP 580 gives.
  • Process safety coordinators. Those who audit mechanical integrity under process safety management need to understand what an RBI-based interval claims and what it does not.

Without one of those inspector certifications, API asks for education plus petrochemical industry experience within the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree or higher, two with a two-year degree, three with a high school diploma and five or more with no formal education. A chemical engineer from LSU's ABET-accredited programme who has worked a year on a corridor unit can usually apply; API decides whether the experience qualifies, so describe it accurately.

The mechanical integrity framework behind RBI on the corridor

Louisiana is not an OSHA State Plan state, so federal OSHA, through its Baton Rouge Area Office, covers most private-sector workplaces here, and the process safety management standard, 29 CFR 1910.119, applies to covered processes. EPA's risk management program rule carries parallel wording in 40 CFR 68.73: inspection frequency must be consistent with applicable manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practices, and more frequent if prior operating experience shows the need. RBI is one recognised way to show that the chosen frequency rests on engineering judgement about damage and consequence rather than on habit.

Two kinds of equipment sit partly outside a plant's RBI freedom, and both appear in corridor registers:

  • Jurisdictional boilers. Louisiana's boiler law runs on certificates issued by the Office of State Fire Marshal: an inspection certificate normally lasts no more than fourteen months, with extensions to two years for certain boilers and five-year certificates where the statute permits. An RBI study can rank a boiler, but the state certificate still governs its inspection.
  • Pipeline breakout tanks. Under 49 CFR 195.432(b), and the matching section of Louisiana's administrative code, breakout tanks are inspected to API 653 except that its risk-based internal inspection procedures cannot set the internal interval. PHMSA published a proposed rule in 2026 that would allow risk-based methods, but a proposal is not law; check whether a final rule exists before relying on it.

The exam itself tests RP 580, not Louisiana law. Knowing where these limits fall still helps, because an RBI assessment does not override jurisdictional requirements, and scope questions can turn on that principle.

Three RBI pictures on one stretch of river

A damage list carried from one plant type to another is the commonest weakness in an RBI study, and the corridor puts three very different plant types within a short drive.

Plant typeCorridor examplesProbability drivers to modelConsequence that tends to dominate
RefiningExxonMobil Baton Rouge; Placid at Port AllenSulfidation, sour water and amine corrosion, hydroprocessing effluent damage, CUI on long insulated runsFlammable release and fire from large hydrocarbon inventories
Chlor-alkali and vinylsDow and Shintech at PlaquemineWet chlorine and hydrochloric acid corrosion, caustic stress corrosion cracking, chloride cracking of stainless steel, lining failureToxic release, which can make a small connection high risk
Ammonia and methanolCF Industries at Donaldsonville; Methanex at GeismarAmmonia stress corrosion cracking, high temperature hydrogen attack in syngas service, CUI on cold and cycling linesToxic ammonia or flammable syngas and methanol

The table describes typical mechanisms for each type of unit, not findings at any named plant. The exam point it illustrates is RP 580's insistence that probability of failure is built from the damage mechanisms actually credible for the equipment, and that consequence is assessed for the fluid, inventory and surroundings, so that two items with similar wall loss can sit in very different risk categories.

The data behind a corridor RBI model, and where it hides

The corridor's plants span more than a century. ExxonMobil's refinery dates from 1909, Dow came to Louisiana in 1956, Shell's Geismar site began operating in 1967 and Placid's Port Allen refinery in 1975. At the other end of the range sit units with design data but little operating history: the polypropylene unit ExxonMobil started at Baton Rouge in 2022, Methanex's third Geismar plant, which made its first methanol in 2024, the ethylene and chlor-alkali units Shintech announced in 2026, and the low-carbon ammonia plant CF Industries, JERA and Mitsui approved in 2025.

Old and new equipment fail an RBI study in different ways. Older items may lack original material certificates, post-weld heat treatment records or a reliable baseline thickness, so the assessment carries more uncertainty and RP 580 expects that uncertainty to show in the result instead of being assumed away. New items have records but no measured corrosion rate, so the first assessment leans on predicted rates and a baseline inspection. API 580 questions often ask what should happen in each case: what data to gather, how to treat missing data, and what should trigger a reassessment.

Reassessment triggers are worth learning as a list: a management of change that alters process conditions or materials, an excursion outside an integrity operating window, a significant inspection finding, a change in feedstock, the end of the planned assessment period and new information about a damage mechanism. API RP 584 covers integrity operating windows; the API 584 summary explains how those limits connect to RBI.

A closed-book example: matching the inspection to the mechanism

API 580 has no calculation section like the inspector certifications, but it tests reasoning that can be practised question by question. Here is an original practice item in the style of the exam.

Question. An RBI register ranks a carbon steel line downstream of a caustic evaporator as high risk, driven by the probability of caustic stress corrosion cracking at welds that were not stress relieved. The last three inspections were UT thickness readings at the existing CMLs, all showing negligible wall loss. Which action most reduces the uncertainty in the assessed probability of failure?

  1. Add more UT thickness CMLs along the line.
  2. Shorten the interval between thickness surveys.
  3. Examine the welds and heat-affected zones with a crack-detection technique suited to stress corrosion cracking, over a defined coverage.
  4. Increase the frequency of external visual inspection.

Answer and reasoning. The third option. Inspection lowers risk mainly by reducing uncertainty about the probability of failure, and it only does that when the technique can find the damage that is expected. Thickness readings measure wall loss, not cracking, so adding more of them or repeating them sooner changes almost nothing about the cracking probability, however clean the results look. External visual inspection cannot see process-side cracks. A crack-detection method applied to the right locations is the only choice that targets the mechanism driving the ranking. RP 581's quantitative method grades this idea as inspection effectiveness, from highly effective down to ineffective, and the exam expects you to recognise when repeated inspection of the wrong kind adds activity without adding knowledge.

How the API 580 examination is built

The exam has 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 scored and 10 unscored pretest items, sat closed-book over 3.25 hours against a set passing scaled score. It is based on the API 580 Body of Knowledge, which draws on API RP 580 and lists the edition examined for each window on the Publications Effectivity Sheet. RP 581 is the quantitative method; study RP 580's framework first and RP 581's terms only as far as the Body of Knowledge asks.

Because nothing can be looked up, the preparation is about understanding rather than navigation: the purpose and limits of RBI, the qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches, probability and consequence and how they combine, inspection planning and effectiveness, roles and responsibilities on the RBI team, documentation, and reassessment. The API 580 course page sets out the Body of Knowledge in more detail.

Studying API 580 next to planning and turnaround work

People who sit API 580 on the corridor are usually already busy with inspection plans, and the turnaround cycle makes some months heavier than others. The self-paced format lets you study the framework in quieter periods and use the busy ones for short reviews. A useful exercise is to take your own site's RBI vocabulary, which comes from whatever software or procedure the plant uses, and map each term to its RP 580 equivalent; exam questions use RP 580's language, and candidates who know only their software's labels lose marks they should have won.

When the two vocabularies do not line up, or a scenario seems to have two right answers, send it to the instructor, who answers from the text of RP 580 so you see why one option is better. Pick your window early from the API exam schedule; Prometric lists test centres in and around Baton Rouge, and API's information for your window says whether remote proctoring is available.

Exam preparation and an RBI study are different jobs

Passing API 580 shows that you understand the method. It does not make anyone an RBI analyst for a particular plant, and it does not authorise anyone to approve inspection intervals; under API 510, 570 and 653 the owner's authorized inspector and engineer remain responsible for that. Some operators on the corridor also commission an outside study, and Atlantis carries out remote RBI studies for Baton Rouge plants and terminals as a separate service from this course. Fitness-for-service assessment is a different discipline again: it stays with the owner's engineer, and Atlantis does not offer it.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from a Baton Rouge site

An inspection or reliability group can enrol several people together under one quote; fees are quoted on request. Each candidate still applies to API individually. Mixed groups work well, for example two certified API 510 inspectors, a corrosion engineer and a planner, because the people who write damage mechanism reviews and the people who execute inspection plans then learn the same framework at the same time.

faq.q: Must I hold API 510 or API 570 before sitting API 580 in Baton Rouge?
faq.a: No. A current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification makes you eligible automatically, but it is not the only route. Without one, API asks for education plus petrochemical industry experience within the last 10 years, from one year with a bachelor's degree to five or more with no formal education. API decides each application.

faq.q: Does experience at a Geismar or Plaquemine chemical plant count as petrochemical industry experience?
faq.a: It may well, but API makes the decision, not the training provider. Describe your role, the plant and the equipment accurately on the application, and if you are unsure whether a particular job qualifies, ask API before you apply. Experience must fall within the last 10 years.

faq.q: Is the API 580 exam open book?
faq.a: No. All 90 questions are answered closed-book within 3.25 hours, so there is no code to search during the exam. Preparation is about understanding RP 580's framework well enough to reason through scenario questions, which is why the course leans on practice questions with explanations rather than navigation drills.

faq.q: Can RBI set the internal inspection interval for a breakout tank at a Louisiana terminal?
faq.a: Not under the current federal rule. 49 CFR 195.432(b), repeated in Louisiana's administrative code, requires breakout tanks to be inspected to API 653 but excludes its risk-based internal interval procedures. PHMSA proposed a change in 2026; until a final rule takes effect, the exclusion stands.

faq.q: Will API 580 teach me the RBI software my site uses?
faq.a: No. The exam is vendor-neutral and built on RP 580, so the course teaches the method and its language rather than any product. That still helps with software, because you will understand what each input represents and why the results move when the data changes.

faq.q: Can I sit API 580 without going to a test centre?
faq.a: Sometimes. API runs API 580 at test centres and, where it offers the option, by remote proctoring; the information for your exam window says which applies. Prometric lists centres in and around Baton Rouge if you prefer to sit in person.

faq.q: Once I pass, what does keeping API 580 certification involve?
faq.a: The certification runs for three years. You can apply to recertify from 90 days before it expires, and a 90-day grace period follows expiry. Unlike the inspector certifications, API does not currently require employment verification to recertify API 580, but check the current rules when your renewal comes round.

faq.q: After an RBI study, who approves the new inspection intervals?
faq.a: The owner does, through its authorized inspector and engineers under API 510, 570 or 653 and the plant's mechanical integrity procedures. An RBI study recommends; it does not approve. Any judgement about continued operation of damaged equipment is a fitness-for-service decision for the owner's engineer.
